idiom_name: hand-written route table of worker callbacks + one render step
implementation_notes: C supplies none of the roles, so the classic structure is written out: a table of {URI pattern -> worker function} is the controller/dispatcher, each worker fills a response model by calling the application layer, and a single render function turns that model into the body. Embedded servers give the pattern its shape without owning it - libmicrohttpd calls one MHD_AccessHandlerCallback for every request (match the url, then answer with MHD_queue_response), and Mongoose delivers MG_EV_HTTP_MSG with a struct mg_http_message that handlers switch on. The explicit split is still the right call when the same model must feed an HTML page and a JSON or plain-text response, or when rendering is done by an in-house template engine; for a handful of endpoints a single dispatch function with inline rendering is enough.
pitfalls: Without a per-request arena, strings owned by the worker must outlive the render step; every pointer placed in the response model needs a lifetime that covers rendering.
A worker that writes the body itself (or calls MHD_queue_response directly) bypasses the render step and reintroduces exactly the coupling the split removes.
Route tables need a sentinel or an explicit element count - an unterminated table walks off the end on every request.
